title: 3Sum Closest
description: Given an integer array `nums` of length n and an integer `target`, find three integers in `nums` such that the sum is closest to `target`. Return the sum of the three integers (assume exactly one solution exists).
hints: Sort the array, then fix the first number and use two pointers on the rest, moving whichever pointer improves the sum's closeness to target.

title: 3Sum Smaller
description: Given an array of `n` integers `nums` and an integer `target`, return the number of index triplets `i < j < k` such that `nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] < target`.
hints: Sort the array, fix the smallest index, then use two pointers: if the sum is small enough, every index between lo and hi also works with nums[i]+nums[lo] fixed — count them all at once and advance lo; otherwise shrink hi.

title: Remove Element
description: Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `val`, remove all occurrences of `val` and return the resulting array (order does not matter).
hints: Keep a write pointer for the next slot to fill; scan through and copy every element that isn't val into that slot.

title: Sort Transformed Array
description: Given a sorted integer array `nums` and quadratic coefficients `a`, `b`, `c`, apply `f(x) = a*x^2 + b*x + c` to every element and return the resulting array sorted in ascending order.
constraints: nums is sorted in ascending order.
hints: Simply apply f to every element and sort the results — the quadratic-shape trick (two pointers from both ends) is only needed for an O(n) solution, but sorting directly is correct and simple.

title: Partition Array According to Given Pivot
description: Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `pivot`, rearrange `nums` such that all elements less than `pivot` come first (in their original relative order), then all elements equal to `pivot`, then all elements greater than `pivot` (in their original relative order). Return the rearranged array.
constraints: pivot equals an element of nums.
hints: A single stable pass collecting less-than, equal-to, and greater-than elements into three separate lists (then concatenating) keeps relative order automatically.

title: Jump Game III
description: Given an array of non-negative integers `arr` and an integer `start`, you start at index `start`. From index `i` you can jump to `i + arr[i]` or `i - arr[i]` (if within bounds). Return `true` if you can reach any index with value `0`.
hints: This is a reachability question on a graph of index-jumps — BFS or DFS from start, marking visited indices to avoid infinite loops.

title: Non-decreasing Array
description: Given an array `nums` with `n` integers, return `true` if it can become non-decreasing by modifying at most one element.
hints: Scan for a violation (nums[i] > nums[i+1]); if more than one occurs, it's impossible.
At the first violation, decide greedily whether to lower nums[i] or raise nums[i+1], based on which keeps the array most flexible (compare against nums[i-1]).

title: Minimum Domino Rotations For Equal Row
description: You have dominoes in a row, given by `tops` and `bottoms` (both length n), where `tops[i]` and `bottoms[i]` are the values on the `i`-th domino. In one move, swap the top and bottom values of one domino. Return the minimum number of moves so that every value in `tops` is the same, or every value in `bottoms` is the same, or `-1` if impossible.
hints: Only the value that appears at position 0 in either tops or bottoms could possibly be the target — try making everything equal to tops[0], and if that fails, try bottoms[0].
For a candidate target value, count how many rotations are needed (whichever side needs fewer flips), failing immediately if some domino has neither side equal to the target.

title: Broken Calculator
description: You start with the integer `startValue` on a broken calculator that only supports multiplying the current number by 2, or subtracting 1 from it. Return the minimum number of operations needed to display `target`.
hints: Work backward from target instead: half it when even (undoing a multiply), or add 1 when odd (undoing a subtract).
Once target drops to or below startValue, every remaining step is a straightforward +1 (undoing subtracts) to close the gap.

title: Bag of Tokens
description: You have `tokens` and starting `power`. For each token, you may either play it face up (costing `tokens[i]` power, gaining 1 score) or face down (requiring score >= 1, gaining `tokens[i]` power, losing 1 score), each token usable once, in any order. Return the maximum score achievable.
hints: Sort the tokens. Greedily play the cheapest token face up whenever you can afford it (to gain score), and when you can't afford anything, play the most expensive remaining token face down (trading score for power) to keep going.
Track the best score seen at any point during this process — you don't have to use every token.

title: Maximize Sum Of Array After K Negations
description: Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`, modify the array by choosing an index and negating its value, exactly `k` times (an index can be chosen multiple times). Return the largest possible sum of the array after exactly `k` negations.
hints: Sort the array and greedily flip the most negative numbers first — each flip on a negative number always increases the sum.
If k negations remain after all negatives are gone, only the smallest absolute value matters: flip it back and forth (equivalent to flipping it once more only if k is odd).

title: Largest Perimeter Triangle
description: Given an integer array `nums`, return the largest perimeter of a triangle with a non-zero area that can be formed using three of these lengths, or `0` if no such triangle exists.
hints: Sort descending and check consecutive triples: the largest valid triangle always uses the largest possible sides, so the first triple satisfying the triangle inequality (a + b > c for the largest side c) is optimal.

title: Car Pooling
description: A car has `capacity` empty seats. Given `trips` where `trips[i] = [numPassengers, from, to]` describes a trip picking up `numPassengers` at km `from` and dropping them at km `to`, return `true` if it's possible to carry all passengers without exceeding capacity at any point.
hints: Use a difference array over the km range: add numPassengers at 'from' and subtract it at 'to'.
Sweep through the difference array, accumulating a running passenger count, and fail as soon as it exceeds capacity.

title: Minimum Number of Refueling Stops
description: A car starts with `startFuel` and must travel `target` miles. Along the way there are `stations`, each `[position, fuel]`. Return the minimum number of refueling stops needed to reach `target`, or `-1` if impossible.
hints: Greedily drive as far as possible, and whenever you would run out of fuel to reach the next station (or the target), use the largest fuel amount from every station already passed — a max-heap of passed stations' fuel values makes this efficient.

title: Furthest Building You Can Reach
description: Given an array `heights`, you start at building 0 with `bricks` and `ladders`. Moving from building `i` to `i+1`: if heights are equal or decreasing, it's free; otherwise you must use bricks (equal to the height difference) or a ladder. Return the furthest building index you can reach.
hints: Greedily use ladders on the biggest climbs you've seen so far: keep a min-heap of climbs paid for with a ladder, and whenever a new climb is bigger than the smallest ladder-covered climb, swap them (pay bricks for the smaller one instead).
Stop as soon as you don't have enough bricks left to cover the smallest ladder-covered climb.

title: Reorganize String
description: Given a string `s`, rearrange its characters so that no two adjacent characters are the same, and return any such rearrangement, or an empty string if impossible.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters.
hints: If any character's count exceeds (length + 1) / 2, it's impossible to avoid adjacent repeats.
Greedily place the currently most frequent character next (skipping the one just placed), using a max-heap of character counts.

title: Meeting Rooms
description: Given an array of meeting time intervals `intervals` where `intervals[i] = [starti, endi]`, return `true` if a person could attend every meeting (no two meetings overlap).
hints: Sort the intervals by start time, then check that every interval's start is at or after the previous interval's end.

title: Trapping Rain Water II
description: Given an `m x n` integer matrix `heightMap` representing terrain elevation, return the total volume of rain water trapped after raining.
hints: Water always leaks out through the boundary, so start a min-heap with every border cell.

Repeatedly pop the lowest 'wall' from the heap, and for each unvisited neighbor, it traps water up to max(current wall height, its own height) — push the neighbor into the heap with that height as its new effective wall.

title: Next Greater Element II
description: Given a circular integer array `nums` (the next element of the last element is the first element), return an array where each element is the next greater number for the corresponding element in `nums`, searching circularly, or `-1` if none exists.
hints: Simulate the circular array by iterating through it twice (indices 0 to 2n-1, using i % n), using a monotonic decreasing stack of indices to resolve each element's next greater value.

title: Continuous Subarray Sum
description: Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`, return `true` if `nums` has a contiguous subarray of length at least 2 whose sum is a multiple of `k` (0 is considered a multiple of every k).
hints: Track the running prefix sum modulo k, and remember the first index at which each remainder was seen.
If the same remainder reappears at an index at least 2 apart from its first occurrence, the subarray between them sums to a multiple of k.

title: Excel Sheet Column Number
description: Given a string `columnTitle` representing a column title as it appears in an Excel sheet (e.g. 'A' -> 1, 'Z' -> 26, 'AA' -> 27), return its corresponding column number.
constraints: columnTitle consists only of uppercase English letters.
hints: This is base-26 conversion, except digits run 1-26 instead of 0-25 — process left to right, result = result*26 + (char value).

title: Excel Sheet Column Title
description: Given an integer `columnNumber`, return its corresponding Excel sheet column title (e.g. 1 -> 'A', 26 -> 'Z', 27 -> 'AA').
hints: This is base-26, but since there's no digit for 0 (letters run 1-26), subtract 1 before taking the remainder at each step.

title: Replace Words
description: Given a `dictionary` of root words and a `sentence`, replace every word in the sentence with the shortest root from the dictionary that it starts with (a word with no such root is left unchanged). Return the resulting sentence.
hints: For each word in the sentence, check every dictionary root (or better, group roots by length and check prefixes shortest-first) to find the shortest matching prefix.

inputs.sentence: the cattle was rattled by the battery

test_cases.expected_output: the cat was rat by the bat

title: Longest Word in Dictionary
description: Given an array of strings `words`, return the longest word that can be built one character at a time by other words in `words` (every prefix of the word, including itself, must exist in `words`). If there are multiple such words with the same length, return the lexicographically smallest. Return an empty string if no such word exists.
constraints: words[i] consists of lowercase English letters.
hints: Sort the words, then keep a set of 'buildable' words: a word qualifies if it's a single letter, or if the word without its last character is already buildable.
Track the best (longest, then lexicographically smallest) buildable word as you go.

title: Repeated String Match
description: Given two strings `a` and `b`, return the minimum number of times `a` must be repeated so that `b` is a substring of the repeated string, or `-1` if no such number exists.
hints: Repeat a enough times so its length is at least the length of b, then check if b appears in it. If not, one more repetition covers the remaining edge cases (since a repeated match can't need more than one extra copy).

title: String Matching in an Array
description: Given an array of string `words`, return every string in `words` that is a substring of another word in the array, in the same relative order they appear.
constraints: words[i] consists of lowercase English letters.
All words in words are unique.
hints: For each word, check whether it's a substring of any other (different) word in the array.

title: Custom Sort String
description: You are given two strings `order` and `s`, where `order`'s characters are all unique. Sort the characters of `s` so that they match the relative order in `order` (characters not in `order` may appear anywhere, at the end). Return the sorted string.
constraints: order and s consist of lowercase English letters.
All characters of order are unique.
hints: Count the frequency of every character in s, then build the result by appending each character in order's sequence that many times, followed by any leftover characters not in order.

title: Find and Replace Pattern
description: Given an array of strings `words` and a string `pattern`, return every word in `words` that matches `pattern` (a bijective letter-to-letter mapping exists from the word to the pattern), in any order.
hints: A word matches the pattern exactly when the sequence of 'first occurrence index of each character' is identical for both strings — this normalizes both to a comparable canonical form.

title: Reverse Only Letters
description: Given a string `s`, reverse only the letters in it (leaving all non-letter characters in their original positions) and return the resulting string.
constraints: s consists of printable ASCII characters.
hints: Two pointers from both ends, skipping non-letters on either side, swapping the letters found.

title: License Key Formatting
description: Given a license key string `s` (alphanumeric characters separated by dashes) and an integer `k`, reformat it so every group has exactly `k` characters except possibly the first group (which can be shorter but not empty), separated by dashes, with all letters uppercase.
hints: Strip out the dashes and uppercase everything first, then insert a dash every k characters counting from the right.

title: Maximum 69 Number
description: Given a positive integer `num` consisting only of digits 6 and 9, return the maximum number achievable by changing at most one digit (6 to 9).
hints: Flipping the leftmost 6 to a 9 always gives the biggest possible increase — no need to consider any other digit.

title: Add Strings
description: Given two non-negative integers `num1` and `num2` represented as strings, return the sum of `num1` and `num2` as a string, without converting the inputs directly to integers.
constraints: num1 and num2 consist of digits only.
Neither has leading zeros, except the number 0 itself.
hints: Add digit by digit from the rightmost end of both strings, tracking a carry, just like elementary-school addition.

title: Minimum Length of String After Deleting Similar Ends
description: Given a string `s` consisting only of characters 'a', 'b', and 'c', repeatedly remove a non-empty prefix and a non-empty suffix that consist of the same character (and don't overlap) until you can't anymore. Return the minimum possible length of the resulting string.
constraints: s consists only of characters 'a', 'b', and 'c'.
hints: Two pointers from both ends: while the characters at both ends match, keep skipping past every occurrence of that character from both sides, then stop once they differ or the pointers meet.

title: Rotate String
description: Given two strings `s` and `goal`, return `true` if and only if `s` can become `goal` after some number of left shifts (rotations).
hints: Every rotation of s is a substring of s + s (when lengths match) — check if goal is a substring of that doubled string.

title: Delete Columns to Make Sorted
description: You are given an array of equal-length strings `strs`. Return the minimum number of columns (character positions) you must delete so that every remaining column is sorted in non-decreasing (lexicographic) order from top to bottom.
constraints: strs[i] consists of lowercase English letters.
hints: Check each column independently: it needs to be deleted if any adjacent pair of rows is out of order at that position.

title: Rectangle Area
description: Given the coordinates of two rectilinear rectangles on a 2D plane (rectangle 1 by bottom-left `(ax1, ay1)` and top-right `(ax2, ay2)`, rectangle 2 by `(bx1, by1)` and `(bx2, by2)`), return the total area covered by the two rectangles.
hints: Total area is areaA + areaB minus their overlap.
The overlap's width is max(0, min(ax2,bx2) - max(ax1,bx1)), and similarly for height; multiply them for the overlap area.

title: Ugly Number
description: An ugly number is a positive integer whose prime factors are limited to `2`, `3`, and `5`. Given an integer `n`, return `true` if it is an ugly number.
hints: Repeatedly divide n by 2, then 3, then 5, as many times as possible; n is ugly exactly when this reduces it to 1 (and n started positive).

title: Ugly Number II
description: An ugly number is a positive integer whose prime factors are limited to `2`, `3`, and `5`. Given an integer `n`, return the `n`-th ugly number.
hints: Build the sequence of ugly numbers in order: maintain three pointers (one per prime factor 2, 3, 5) into the sequence built so far, and at each step take the minimum of ugly[p2]*2, ugly[p3]*3, ugly[p5]*5 as the next ugly number, advancing whichever pointer(s) produced it.

title: Super Ugly Number
description: A super ugly number is a positive integer whose prime factors are all in the given array `primes`. Given an integer `n` and `primes`, return the `n`-th super ugly number.
hints: Generalize Ugly Number II: keep one pointer per prime into the sequence built so far, and at each step take the minimum of (ugly[pointer[i]] * primes[i]) across all primes, advancing every pointer that produced that minimum.

title: Add Digits
description: Given an integer `num`, repeatedly add all its digits together until the result has only one digit, and return that digit.
hints: Repeatedly summing digits until one remains is the 'digital root', which has a direct formula: 0 if num is 0, otherwise 1 + (num - 1) mod 9.

title: Perfect Number
description: A perfect number is a positive integer equal to the sum of its positive divisors, excluding itself. Given an integer `num`, return `true` if it is a perfect number.
hints: Only check divisors up to sqrt(num), adding both a divisor and its pair (num / divisor) whenever you find one.

title: Self Dividing Numbers
description: A self-dividing number is divisible by every digit it contains (and contains no zero digit). Given a range `[left, right]`, return the list of every self-dividing number in that range, in order.
hints: For each number, check every digit: it must be non-zero and evenly divide the number.

title: Water and Jug Problem
description: You have jugs of capacity `x` liters and `y` liters, and an unlimited water supply. Determine if you can measure out exactly `target` liters using these two jugs (fill, empty, or pour one jug into the other).
hints: By Bezout's identity, the amounts reachable using two jugs of capacity x and y are exactly the multiples of gcd(x, y) up to x + y.
So the answer is true exactly when target <= x + y and target is divisible by gcd(x, y) (with target == 0 always achievable).

title: Integer Replacement
description: Given a positive integer `n`, in one operation you may replace `n` with `n + 1`, or (if `n` is even) `n / 2`. Return the minimum number of operations needed to reduce `n` to 1.
hints: If n is even, always halve it. If n is odd, look at the second-to-last bit: it's usually better to add 1 (letting you halve twice), except at n == 3 where subtracting is better — comparing (n+1) and (n-1) bit patterns handles this uniformly.

title: Bulb Switcher
description: There are `n` bulbs, all initially off. On the `i`-th round (1-indexed), you toggle every bulb whose index is a multiple of `i`. Return the number of bulbs that are on after `n` rounds.
hints: A bulb ends up on exactly when it has an odd number of divisors, which happens only for perfect squares.
So the answer is simply the number of perfect squares up to n, which is floor(sqrt(n)).

title: Paint House
description: There are `n` houses in a row, each to be painted red, blue, or green. `costs[i] = [costRed, costBlue, costGreen]` is the cost of painting house `i` each color. No two adjacent houses may be the same color. Return the minimum total cost to paint all houses.
hints: dp[i][c] = minimum cost to paint the first i+1 houses with house i colored c.
dp[i][c] = costs[i][c] + min(dp[i-1][other colors]).

title: Paint Fence
description: You are painting a fence of `n` posts with `k` colors. Return the number of ways to paint the fence such that no more than two adjacent posts have the same color.
hints: Track two running counts: ways ending with the last post a different color from the one before it ('diff'), and ways ending with the last two posts the same color ('same').
Each step: new 'same' = old 'diff' (you can only repeat if the previous two differed); new 'diff' = (old 'same' + old 'diff') * (k - 1).

title: Wiggle Subsequence
description: A wiggle sequence is one where consecutive differences strictly alternate between positive and negative. Given an integer array `nums`, return the length of the longest wiggle subsequence.
hints: Track two running lengths: the longest wiggle subsequence ending with an upward move, and one ending with a downward move.
Whenever the current element is greater than the previous, 'up' can extend from 'down' + 1 (and vice versa for 'down').

title: Longest Common Substring
description: Given two strings `text1` and `text2`, return the length of their longest common substring (a contiguous run of characters common to both strings).
constraints: text1 and text2 consist of lowercase English letters.
hints: Unlike the subsequence version, a mismatch resets the run to 0 rather than carrying forward the best of two neighbors.
dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1] + 1 if text1[i-1] == text2[j-1], else 0. Track the maximum dp value seen anywhere.

title: Maximum Product of Word Lengths
description: Given a string array `words`, return the maximum value of `length(words[i]) * length(words[j])` over all pairs where the two words share no common letters. Return 0 if no such pair exists.
constraints: words[i] consists only of lowercase English letters.
hints: Represent each word's letter set as a 26-bit bitmask.
Two words share no letters exactly when their bitmasks AND to zero — check every pair of masks.

title: Minimum Number of Removals to Make Mountain Array
description: Given an integer array `nums`, return the minimum number of elements to remove to make the remaining array a mountain array (strictly increasing then strictly decreasing, with at least one element on each side of the peak).
constraints: It is guaranteed that a valid mountain array exists after some removals.
hints: For every index, compute the longest strictly increasing subsequence ending there, and the longest strictly decreasing subsequence starting there.

An index can be the peak only if both of those are at least 2; the best mountain length using it as peak is (increasing length + decreasing length - 1). Minimize removals as n minus the best mountain length.

title: Arithmetic Slices
description: An array is arithmetic if it has at least 3 elements and consecutive differences are all equal. Given an integer array `nums`, return the number of arithmetic subarrays (contiguous) of length 3 or more.
hints: Track a running count of how many arithmetic slices end at the current index — extending an existing arithmetic run by one element adds that many new slices (plus one) to the total.

title: Arithmetic Slices II - Subsequence
description: Given an integer array `nums`, return the number of arithmetic subsequences (not necessarily contiguous, length 3 or more, constant common difference) in it.
hints: For each index i, keep a hash map from common-difference to the count of arithmetic subsequences of length >= 2 ending at i with that difference.

When extending from an earlier index j to i (difference d = nums[i]-nums[j]), every length->=2 sequence ending at j with difference d extends to a length->=3 sequence ending at i — add dp[j][d] to the total, and dp[i][d] accumulates dp[j][d] + 1 (the +1 counts the new length-2 pair itself).

title: Count Vowels Permutation
description: Given an integer `n`, count how many strings of length `n` can be formed using vowels ('a','e','i','o','u') under these rules: 'a' may only be followed by 'e'; 'e' may only be followed by 'a' or 'i'; 'i' may be followed by any vowel except 'i'; 'o' may only be followed by 'i' or 'u'; 'u' may only be followed by 'a'. Return the count modulo `10^9 + 7`.
hints: Track the count of strings ending in each vowel at each length, using the transition rules to determine which counts feed into which for the next length.

title: Shortest Common Supersequence Length
description: Given two strings `str1` and `str2`, return the length of the shortest string that has both `str1` and `str2` as subsequences.
constraints: str1 and str2 consist of lowercase English letters.
hints: The shortest common supersequence length is len(str1) + len(str2) - LCS(str1, str2) — every character not shared between the two strings must appear, plus one copy of every shared character.

title: Interleaving String
description: Given strings `s1`, `s2`, and `s3`, return `true` if `s3` is formed by an interleaving of `s1` and `s2` (a merge of both strings, in order, using every character of each exactly once).
hints: If len(s1) + len(s2) != len(s3), it's impossible immediately.
dp[i][j] = whether s3[:i+j] can be formed from s1[:i] and s2[:j]; it's true if (dp[i-1][j] and s1[i-1]==s3[i+j-1]) or (dp[i][j-1] and s2[j-1]==s3[i+j-1]).

title: Minimum ASCII Delete Sum for Two Strings
description: Given two strings `s1` and `s2`, return the lowest total ASCII sum of characters you must delete from both strings to make them equal.
constraints: s1 and s2 consist of lowercase English letters.
hints: dp[i][j] = minimum ASCII delete sum to equalize s1[:i] and s2[:j].
If the last characters match, dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1]; otherwise it's the cheaper of deleting s1's last character or s2's last character.

title: Largest Plus Sign
description: You have an `n x n` grid of all 1's, except for cells listed in `mines` (each `[row, col]`) which are 0. Return the order of the largest axis-aligned plus sign of 1's that can be found in the grid (0 if none).
hints: For each cell, compute how far it can extend as consecutive 1's in each of the 4 directions (left, right, up, down) using running counts that reset at a mine.
A cell's plus-sign order is the minimum of its 4 directional reach counts (including itself); track the overall maximum.

title: Number of Dice Rolls With Target Sum
description: You have `n` dice, each with `k` faces numbered 1 to `k`. Return the number of ways to roll the dice so the values sum to `target`, modulo `10^9 + 7`.
hints: dp[dice][sum] = number of ways to reach sum using that many dice.
For each additional die, try every face value 1..k and add dp[dice-1][sum - face] to dp[dice][sum].

title: Profitable Schemes
description: You have `n` members. Given `group` and `profit` arrays where crime `i` requires `group[i]` members and yields `profit[i]` profit, and a `minProfit` target, return the number of distinct schemes (subsets of crimes) using at most `n` members total that generate at least `minProfit`, modulo `10^9 + 7`.
hints: This is a 2D knapsack: dp[members][profitSoFar] = number of schemes, where profitSoFar is capped at minProfit (any profit beyond the target counts the same as exactly hitting it).
For each crime, update dp from high member-count down to low, and for the profit dimension, add to min(current + profit[i], minProfit).

title: Minimum Time to Make Rope Colorful
description: You have a rope of balloons represented by `colors`, where adjacent balloons of the same color must be removed until no two adjacent balloons share a color; removing a balloon takes `neededTime[i]` seconds. Return the minimum time needed.
hints: Process the string in runs of the same color: within any run, keep the balloon with the highest removal time (cheapest to keep) and remove all the others.

title: Maximum Alternating Subsequence Sum
description: The alternating sum of a subsequence is `sub[0] - sub[1] + sub[2] - sub[3] + ...`. Given an integer array `nums`, return the maximum alternating sum of any subsequence (choosing which elements to include and their order preserved).
hints: Track two running states: the best alternating sum ending on an 'even position' (added) term, and ending on an 'odd position' (subtracted) term.
At each element, either skip it (carry forward) or include it, updating whichever state benefits from adding or subtracting the current value.

title: Count Number of Teams
description: You have `n` soldiers with distinct ratings in `rating`. Count the number of ways to choose 3 soldiers `i < j < k` such that `rating[i] < rating[j] < rating[k]` or `rating[i] > rating[j] > rating[k]`.
hints: For each middle soldier j, count how many soldiers to its left are smaller/larger, and how many to its right are smaller/larger.
Combine those counts: (left smaller * right larger) + (left larger * right smaller) gives the teams centered at j.

title: Minimum Swaps to Make Sequences Increasing
description: Given two equal-length integer arrays `nums1` and `nums2`, in one operation you may swap `nums1[i]` and `nums2[i]` at the same index. Return the minimum number of swaps to make both arrays strictly increasing.
hints: Track two running values at each index: the minimum swaps if index i is NOT swapped, and if it IS swapped, for both arrays to be strictly increasing up to that point.
At each step, check both the 'no swap needed' transition (values already increasing without touching this index) and the 'both indices swapped' transition, taking the best that keeps validity.

title: Redundant Connection II
description: A rooted tree with `n` nodes had one extra directed edge added, given as `edges` (each `[parent, child]`), possibly giving one node two parents or creating a cycle. Return the single edge that can be removed so the remaining edges form a valid rooted tree with all nodes reachable from the root.
hints: First check if any node has two parents — if so, remember both candidate edges giving it a second parent.

Run Union-Find over all edges, skipping the second candidate edge if one exists. If a cycle still forms, the first candidate edge is the answer; otherwise, the second candidate edge (or, if no node ever had two parents, whichever edge Union-Find first detects as forming a cycle) is the answer.

title: Satisfiability of Equality Equations
description: Given an array of strings `equations` (each of the form `"a==b"` or `"a!=b"`, with single lowercase-letter variables), return `true` if it's possible to assign values to the variables so that all equations are satisfied.
constraints: equations[i] is of the form 'x==y' or 'x!=y'.
hints: Union every pair connected by '==' first — equality is transitive.
Then check every '!=' equation: if both variables ended up in the same union-find component, the constraints are contradictory.

title: Path with Maximum Probability
description: Given an undirected graph of `n` nodes, `edges` (each `[a, b]`), and `succProb[i]` the success probability of traversing `edges[i]`, return the maximum probability of success to travel from `start` to `end`, or `0` if no path exists.
hints: This is Dijkstra's algorithm, but maximizing a product of probabilities instead of minimizing a sum of distances — use a max-heap keyed on probability.

title: Minimum Cost to Connect Sticks
description: You have sticks with lengths given by `sticks`. Connecting two sticks of lengths `x` and `y` costs `x + y`, producing one stick of length `x + y`. Return the minimum total cost to connect all sticks into one.
hints: Greedily always combine the two currently-shortest sticks — a min-heap makes this efficient.
Repeat until only one stick remains, summing every combination cost along the way.

title: Remove Max Number of Edges to Keep Graph Fully Traversable
description: Alice and Bob have a graph of `n` nodes with three edge types: type 1 (Alice only), type 2 (Bob only), type 3 (both). Given `edges` (each `[type, u, v]`), return the maximum number of edges that can be removed while the graph remains fully traversable by both Alice and Bob, or `-1` if it's impossible for both to fully traverse it.
hints: Process type-3 edges first, adding each to BOTH Alice's and Bob's Union-Find structures whenever it actually connects two different components.

Then process type-1 edges into Alice's structure and type-2 into Bob's, counting every edge that was actually needed. If either structure doesn't end up fully connected (n-1 union operations), return -1; otherwise the answer is total edges minus edges actually used.

title: Count Sub Islands
description: Given two `m x n` binary grids `grid1` and `grid2`, an island in `grid2` is considered a sub-island if every cell of that island is also land in `grid1`. Return the number of sub-islands in `grid2`.
hints: For each island in grid2, flood-fill it and check whether every visited cell is also land (1) in grid1 — if any cell fails, it's not a sub-island, but keep flood-filling to mark the whole island visited regardless.

title: Shortest Bridge
description: Given a binary matrix `grid` containing exactly two islands (each a group of 4-directionally connected 1's), return the minimum number of 0's you must flip to 1 to connect the two islands.
hints: DFS from any land cell to find and mark the entire first island.
Then multi-source BFS from every cell of that island outward over water, expanding one ring at a time, until you first reach a cell of the second island — the number of rings expanded is the answer.

title: Walls and Gates
description: You are given an `m x n` grid `rooms` where `-1` marks a wall, `0` marks a gate, and `2147483647` marks an empty room. Fill each empty room with the distance to its nearest gate (leave it as `2147483647` if no gate can reach it). Return the updated grid.
hints: Multi-source BFS starting from every gate at once finds the nearest-gate distance for every reachable room in a single pass.

title: Minimum Obstacle Removal to Reach Corner
description: Given an `m x n` grid `grid` where `0` is an empty cell and `1` is an obstacle, return the minimum number of obstacles to remove to travel from the top-left to the bottom-right corner (moving 4-directionally).
hints: This is a 0-1 BFS: moving into an empty cell costs 0, moving into an obstacle costs 1.
Use a deque: push 0-cost moves to the front and 1-cost moves to the back, so the deque always processes cells in true shortest-cost order.

title: Spiral Matrix III
description: You start at `(rStart, cStart)` in an `rows x cols` grid, facing east, and walk in a clockwise spiral, visiting every position (expanding the spiral even outside grid bounds, but only recording positions inside the grid) until all `rows * cols` grid cells have been visited. Return the list of visited grid positions in order.
hints: Walk the spiral by alternating direction (east, south, west, north) with leg lengths increasing by 1 every two turns, recording only the positions that land inside the grid.

title: Number of Closed Islands
description: Given a binary grid `grid` where `0` represents land and `1` represents water, an island is closed if it's completely surrounded by water (not touching the grid border). Return the number of closed islands.
hints: First flood-fill away every land region touching the border — those can never be closed.
Then count the number of remaining separate land regions.

title: Max Increase to Keep City Skyline
description: Given an `n x n` grid `grid` of building heights, increase the height of any number of buildings such that the skyline viewed from each of the four cardinal directions remains unchanged. Return the maximum total sum of increases possible.
hints: Compute the maximum height in every row and every column first — those are the skyline caps.
Each building can be raised up to min(its row's max, its column's max); sum the increases.

title: Valid Tic-Tac-Toe State
description: Given a 3x3 Tic-Tac-Toe `board` array of strings (each row a 3-character string of 'X', 'O', or ' '), return `true` if the board could be reached by playing a valid game (players alternate turns, X goes first, play stops once someone wins).
hints: Count X's and O's: X count must equal O count, or be exactly one more (since X moves first).
Check who has won (if anyone): O can't have won unless the counts are equal; X can't have won unless X has exactly one more mark than O. Also, both players can't have simultaneously won.

title: Special Positions in a Binary Matrix
description: Given an `m x n` binary matrix `mat`, return the number of special positions — a cell `(i, j)` where `mat[i][j] == 1` and every other cell in row `i` and column `j` is `0`.
hints: Precompute the sum of each row and each column.
A cell (i,j) with value 1 is special exactly when its row sum and column sum are both exactly 1.

title: Factor Combinations
description: Given an integer `n`, return every way to factor it into a combination of factors, each at least 2, in non-decreasing order per combination (excluding the trivial factorization `[n]` itself).
hints: Backtrack starting from factor 2 upward: at each step, try every factor from the current minimum up to sqrt(remaining), recursing on the quotient with that factor as the new minimum, and also record the remaining value itself as the final factor of the current combination.

title: Numbers With Same Consecutive Differences
description: Given integers `n` and `k`, return every positive integer with exactly `n` digits (no leading zero) such that every pair of consecutive digits differs by exactly `k`, in any order.
hints: Backtrack digit by digit, starting each number with digits 1-9 (no leading zero), and at each step branching into the two digits (current +/- k) that are valid (0-9), avoiding duplicates when k is 0.

title: Gray Code
description: An n-bit gray code sequence is a sequence of `2^n` integers where every integer is in the range `[0, 2^n - 1]`, the first is 0, every integer appears exactly once, and adjacent integers (including the last and first) differ in exactly one bit. Given `n`, return a valid n-bit gray code sequence.
hints: There's a direct formula: the i-th gray code value is i XOR (i right-shifted by 1) — no search needed.

title: Expression Add Operators
description: Given a string `num` containing only digits and an integer `target`, return every way to insert the binary operators `+`, `-`, or `*` between the digits of `num` (without altering digit order or adding leading zeros to any operand) so that the resulting expression evaluates to `target`, in any order.
hints: Backtrack, choosing where to split off the next operand (skipping splits that would create a leading zero) and which operator precedes it.
Track the running total AND the value of the last operand separately — multiplication needs to 'undo' the last addition/subtraction before applying itself, since it binds tighter.

title: Next Greater Element III
description: Given a positive integer `n`, find the smallest integer strictly greater than `n` that has exactly the same digits (a permutation of n's digits). Return it, or `-1` if no such integer exists within the 32-bit signed integer range.
hints: This is exactly the 'next permutation' algorithm applied to n's digits: find the rightmost ascent, swap with the smallest larger digit to its right, then reverse the suffix.
If n's digits are already in fully descending order, no larger permutation exists — return -1. Also check the 32-bit bound at the end.

title: Remove Duplicate Letters
description: Given a string `s`, remove duplicate letters so that every letter appears exactly once, and return the result arranged to be the smallest possible in lexicographic order among all valid orderings, keeping each remaining letter's relative order.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters.
hints: Track the last index at which each character occurs, and use a monotonic stack: pop a character off the stack if the new character is smaller, the top can still appear again later, and the top isn't already used elsewhere in the result.

title: Validate Stack Sequences
description: Given two integer arrays `pushed` and `popped`, each a permutation of the same distinct values, return `true` if this could have been the result of a sequence of push and pop operations on an initially empty stack.
constraints: pushed and popped are permutations of each other with distinct values.
hints: Simulate it directly with an actual stack: push values from `pushed` in order, and after each push, pop as many times as possible while the stack's top matches the next expected value in `popped`.
At the end, the sequence is valid exactly when the stack is empty.

title: Dota2 Senate
description: In a Dota2 senate, each senator is either Radiant ('R') or Dire ('D'), given as string `senate`. In rounds, each senator (in order) may ban one senator from the opposing party from all future rounds; the process repeats until only one party remains, which then wins. Return the winning party, `"Radiant"` or `"Dire"`.
hints: Use two queues of indices, one per party. Compare the front of each queue: the earlier-indexed senator bans the later one (removing it), and the surviving senator re-joins the back of their own queue, at index + n (to preserve relative turn order across rounds).

title: Crawler Log Folder
description: A crawler starts in the main folder and executes `logs`: `"../"` moves to the parent folder (no-op at main), `"./"` stays in the current folder, and any other string moves into that subfolder. Return the minimum number of `"../"` operations needed to return to the main folder after executing all logs.
constraints: logs[i] contains lowercase English letters, digits, '.', and '/'.
hints: Just track the current folder depth as a counter: increment for a subfolder move, decrement (not below 0) for '../', and leave it unchanged for './'.
The final depth is exactly the number of '../' operations needed to get back to main.

title: Build an Array With Stack Operations
description: Given a target array `target` (values in strictly increasing order) and an integer `n` (values available from `1` to `n`), build `target` using a stream `1, 2, ..., n` and, for each value, either "Push" it onto the stack, or "Push" then immediately "Pop" it if it's not needed. Return the list of operations ("Push" or "Push Pop") used, stopping once `target` is fully built.
hints: Walk through numbers 1 to n: if the current number is the next needed value in target, record 'Push' and advance to the next target value; otherwise record 'Push Pop' (skip it) and don't advance.
Stop as soon as every value in target has been matched.

title: Distribute Candies
description: Given an even-length integer array `candyType` representing candy types, Alice wants to eat exactly half the candies, distributed among the smallest and least kids alike... simply: return the maximum number of distinct candy types Alice can eat while eating exactly `candyType.length / 2` candies.
hints: Alice can eat at most n/2 candies total, and at most one of each distinct type — so the answer is the minimum of (number of distinct types) and (n/2).

title: Widest Vertical Area Between Two Points Containing No Points
description: Given `points` where `points[i] = [xi, yi]`, return the widest empty vertical area's width — a vertical band with no points strictly inside, bounded by two of the given x-coordinates, excluding the leftmost and rightmost edges of the whole point set.
hints: Sort the distinct x-coordinates, then the answer is the maximum gap between consecutive x-coordinates.

title: Minimum Value to Get Positive Step by Step Sum
description: Given an array of integers `nums`, you choose a positive integer `startValue`, then iterate through `nums`, adding each value to a running sum starting at `startValue`. Return the minimum `startValue` such that the running sum never drops below 1 at any point.
hints: Compute the running prefix sum of nums (without startValue) and find its minimum value.
The answer is 1 - (that minimum), or 1 if the minimum prefix sum is already >= 0.

title: Check if a String Contains All Binary Codes of Size K
description: Given a binary string `s` and an integer `k`, return `true` if every binary code of length `k` (i.e. every number from `0` to `2^k - 1` in binary) is a substring of `s`.
hints: Slide a window of length k across s, collecting every distinct substring seen into a set.
The answer is true exactly when that set's size reaches 2^k.

title: Sum of Square Numbers
description: Given a non-negative integer `c`, return `true` if there exist two integers `a` and `b` such that `a^2 + b^2 == c`.
hints: Two pointers: start a at 0 and b at floor(sqrt(c)), and move inward — increase a if the sum of squares is too small, decrease b if too large.

title: Shortest Distance to a Character
description: Given a string `s` and a character `c` that occurs in `s` at least once, return an array `answer` where `answer[i]` is the shortest distance from index `i` to any occurrence of `c` in `s`.
constraints: c occurs at least once in s.
hints: Two passes: scan left to right tracking distance since the last occurrence of c, then scan right to left doing the same and taking the minimum of both passes at each index.

title: Binary Gap
description: Given a positive integer `n`, return the longest distance between any two adjacent `1`'s in its binary representation, or `0` if there aren't two such `1`'s.
hints: Record the positions of every set bit, then find the maximum difference between consecutive positions.

title: Reordered Power of 2
description: Given a positive integer `n`, return `true` if some reordering of its digits (with no leading zero) forms a power of two.
hints: Two numbers are reorderings of each other exactly when their sorted digit sequences match.
Since n has at most 10 digits, just check every power of two up to 10 digits long and compare sorted digit sequences.

title: Smallest Range Covering Elements from K Lists
description: Given `k` sorted integer lists as `nums` (an array of arrays), return the smallest range `[lo, hi]` such that every one of the k lists has at least one number within that range (inclusive).
hints: Use a min-heap holding one pointer per list, always advancing whichever list has the current smallest value.
Track the current maximum value across the heap; every time you advance, the range [heap min, current max] is a candidate — keep the smallest one seen.

title: Partition Array into Disjoint Intervals
description: Given an integer array `nums`, partition it into two contiguous parts `left` and `right` such that every element in `left` is less than or equal to every element in `right`, `left` and `right` are non-empty, and `left` has the smallest possible length. Return the length of `left`.
hints: Track the maximum value seen so far, and the maximum value within the current candidate 'left' partition.
Whenever you find a value smaller than the left-partition's max, the partition boundary must extend to include it — expand left's max to the overall max-so-far and move the boundary.

title: DI String Match
description: A permutation of `0` to `n` (where `n` is the length of string `s`) is described by `s`, consisting of 'I' (increasing, next number is bigger) and 'D' (decreasing, next number is smaller). Return any valid permutation matching `s`.
hints: Greedily assign the smallest remaining number on 'I' and the largest remaining number on 'D', tracking a low and high pointer starting at 0 and n.

title: Check If N and Its Double Exist
description: Given an array `arr` of integers, return `true` if there exist two distinct indices `i` and `j` such that `arr[i] == 2 * arr[j]`.
hints: Scan through, checking (for each element) whether double it or half it (if evenly divisible) has already been seen; add the current element to the seen set afterward.
